summary: Addendum §3 is built. Uploads, generation outputs (videos via up to 30 ffmpeg keyframes at 1 fps), seed media and backfilled media all go through scanAsset(). There are three adapters: dev (labeled demo, matches only test hashes and a drill fixture, refused in production), PhotoDNA (JPEG, throttled, fails closed on any unexpected reply) and Cloudflare (edge-only, so it returns unavailable when fail-closed is on). Only assets marked clean are served, signed, used as inputs, downloaded or published. Pending assets get the same 404 as deleted ones. On a match the file goes on legal hold and is never purged. The owner is suspended and signed out, and the system adds a csam_match flag, opens an escalation and writes audit rows. The upload reply is a generic 403. A matched output fails with content_blocked and the credits are returned. If the scanner is down with fail-closed on, an upload is deleted and gets a 503; an output is requeued with its credits still reserved, and after a limited number of tries it fails and the credits are refunded. Admins work from /admin/review, where they can confirm a match and record the report reference, or clear a false positive and reinstate the owner. There is a public takedown form at /policies/takedown that works without an account, with an admin queue for action or dismissal. docs/abuse-response.md is the runbook. 19 new integration tests; 140/140 tests pass overall.

docsNotes:
PIPELINE: every asset gets media_assets.scan_status (pending|clean|matched|unavailable; default pending) plus scan_provider, scan_ref, scanned_at and legal_hold (migration 0002). scanAsset(subject) runs at: upload (after WebP re-encode; the hash of the received bytes is passed as sourceSha256 so known-hash lists match the original), each generation output before it is attached (videos: ffmpeg fps=1, at most 30 keyframes, each scanned; a poster inherits its clip's verdict as 'derived:<clipId>'), seed (origin 'seed'; seeding stops unless clean), and scripts/scan-backfill.ts (pending, plus unavailable with --include-unavailable; exits 1 if anything is left pending or unavailable). e2e-prepare runs the backfill after seeding. Existing databases MUST run `npx tsx scripts/scan-backfill.ts` once, because pending assets are no longer served.

SERVING RULE: only 'clean' is signed (assetUrl), served (/api/media gives the same 404 as a deleted asset, even with a link signed earlier), downloaded, accepted as a generation input, or published (409 not_cleared 'This creation hasn't cleared our safety checks, so it can't be published.'; the output and the poster are both checked).

VERDICT TABLE: clean -> normal. matched/upload -> asset kept on legal hold (never purged, skipped by consent withdrawal, account deletion and both purge paths); owner suspended and their sessions deleted; account_flags csam_match; moderation escalate event (reason csam_match); audits scan.block and user.suspend; reply is a generic 403 upload_rejected 'This upload was rejected.' matched/output -> same hold, flag and escalation; job fails with content_blocked 'This creation was blocked by our safety checks. Your credits were returned.'; no output row; earlier outputs from the same job are deleted. A repeat scan of an already matched asset opens no second case. unavailable -> see fail-closed. The generic tools refuse escalations: resolveReport and clearFlag on csam_match return 409 use_review_queue; the admin flags list links to /admin/review instead; escalations are kept out of the open-reports count and the moderation queue.

FAIL-CLOSED (SCAN_FAIL_CLOSED=true, default): a scanner error, timeout (SCAN_TIMEOUT_S), missing configuration or unexpected reply means unavailable. Upload: uploads row and consent record deleted, asset soft-deleted, bytes purged; 503 scan_unavailable 'We couldn't check this file right now. Try again in a few minutes.' Output: stored files deleted, job requeued with its reservation kept, BullMQ backoff, and after maxAttempts (3) it fails with scan_unavailable and the credits are refunded. Seed: throws. Fail-open (false): kept as 'unavailable', never served or used, rescanned with backfill --include-unavailable. env() refuses SCAN_PROVIDER=dev in production when fail-closed is on, and the dev provider also returns unavailable in production.

PROVIDERS: dev = demo scanner; matches SCAN_DEV_MATCH_HASHES plus the built-in fixture hash 74e83d5d...a184 (tests/fixtures/scan-drill-match.png); SCAN_DEV_SIMULATE_OUTAGE=true for drills; setDevScanOverride() hook for tests. photodna = PHOTODNA_API_KEY + PHOTODNA_ENDPOINT (no default endpoint guessed). cloudflare = edge-only: returns unavailable when fail-closed, otherwise clean with ref 'edge-only:not-pre-scanned'. CLOUDFLARE_SCAN_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unused (the tool has no webhook). The admin page shows a 'Development scanner · not live' demo badge, plus badges for no pre-storage scan, not configured and the fail-closed state.

REVIEW: /admin/review (admin only, otherwise 404); GET /api/admin/review; POST /api/admin/review/[id] {action:'confirm', reportRef, reportedTo: ncmec_cybertipline|iwf|other_authority, note?} keeps the hold, writes a 'hold' event and audit scan.match_confirmed; {action:'clear', note>=3} marks the asset clean ('review-cleared:<id>'), lifts the hold, clears the matching flags, reinstates the owner if no other csam_match flag is open, and audits scan.false_positive_cleared and user.reinstate. Resolving twice gives 409. Templates removed by a match are NOT restored on clear.

TAKEDOWNS: public form at /policies/takedown (no account needed; ?target= prefill; linked from /policies#abuse, the template report sheet and the age gate). POST /api/takedowns: categories ncii, likeness, csam, copyright, other; a good-faith checkbox is required; signed-out requests need an email (422 email_required); 10 per hour per user or IP (429). Admin: GET /api/admin/takedowns?status=open|closed (urgent first); POST /api/admin/takedowns/[id] {action:'action'|'dismiss', note} (dismiss needs a note, 422 note_required; an unresolvable target gives 422 target_not_found). 'Take it down' soft-deletes the target; ncii and likeness purge the files immediately; csam instead holds the files and opens a csam_report escalation. Audits: takedown.create (ids and category only), takedown.action, takedown.dismiss.

Nothing logs media bytes or prompts. Scanner logs carry only asset ids, hashes and the provider.

Reinstate rule: the owner is reinstated only if no other csam_match flag is open. Confirm that is the intended policy.

Should public media become edge-cacheable so Cloudflare's tool can actually see it?
